statement: Fix 1 > p1 > p2 > 0. There is a constant a(p1, p2) > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, if integers m1, m2 satisfy sn(m1) ≥ p1 and sn(m2) ≤ p2, then m2 − m1 ≥ a(p1, p2) √ n.
